- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model underestimates upward momentum; add 2–4% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging with 18d history for lagged corrections.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model delays reaction; shift forecast up by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70.5), model tends to hold or overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (±0.4+), model overfits noise; apply 10% smoothing filter to forecast series.
